encounters.cc: Two-day history of fever, dysuria, and left-sided flank pain in patient with history of pregnancy-related UTIs

lines: Two-day history of fever, dysuria, and left-sided flank pain in patient with history of pregnancy-related UTIs

This 35-year-old female with a known urethral diverticulum and history of acute pyelonephritis in March 2022 returns to the emergency department with a 2-day history of fever, dysuria, and left-sided flank pain.
She reports a history of recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs) during her first trimester, for which she was treated with nitrofurantoin.
On further questioning, she mentions experiencing increased urinary frequency and urgency over the past week.
- Secondary hyperparathyroidism due to vitamin D deficiency (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of recurrent urinary tract infections
Her past surgical history is notable for a laparoscopic appendectomy 5 years ago, with an uncomplicated recovery.
She has been compliant with her prenatal vitamins and iron supplementation, but denies any recent medication changes.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours PRN for wheezing/shortness of breath
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) PO daily with food
- Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 2000 international units PO daily
Physical examination reveals a temperature of 38.5°C (101.3°F), blood pressure of 110/70 mm Hg, and pulse of 98 beats/min.
Tenderness is noted on palpation of the left costovertebral angle.
Laboratory studies reveal a white blood cell count of 14,000/mm³, and a urinalysis positive for leukocyte esterase and nitrites.
Renal ultrasound shows no evidence of hydronephrosis or renal stones.

encounters.cc: Sudden throat tightness, dizziness, and impending doom during intravenous antibiotic infusion for right-sided pyelonephritis

lines: Sudden throat tightness, dizziness, and impending doom during intravenous antibiotic infusion for right-sided pyelonephritis

The patient is a 36-year-old female with a history of urethral diverticulum and recurrent urinary tract infections, including prior episodes of pyelonephritis in 2022, who presents with symptoms for the past 2 days.
She is diagnosed with pyelonephritis and is started on intravenous ceftriaxone after confirming no prior history of reaction to this drug.
Ten minutes into the infusion, she suddenly complains of throat tightness, dizziness, and a sensation of impending doom.
Her voice becomes hoarse, and she begins to cough forcefully.
She then develops generalized flushing, and her face and lips appear swollen.
- Secondary hyperparathyroidism due to vitamin D deficiency (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of recurrent urinary tract infections
She has had multiple urinary tract infections in the past.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours PRN for wheezing/shortness of breath
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) PO daily with food
- Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 2000 international units PO daily
On presentation, she is febrile to 38.9°C (102.0°F).
Vital signs show a temperature of 37.2°C (99°F), pulse of 132/min, respirations of 28/min, and blood pressure of 68/42 mm Hg.
Her oxygen saturation drops to 91% on room air.
Physical examination reveals periorbital and lip edema, diffuse erythematous urticarial plaques over her chest and arms, and bilateral expiratory wheezes and inspiratory stridor.
She appears anxious and is using accessory muscles to breathe.
Jugular venous pressure is not elevated, and cardiac exam reveals tachycardia without murmurs.
There is no peripheral edema or signs of fluid overload.
Urinalysis shows pyuria, positive leukocyte esterase, and nitrites
Started on intravenous ceftriaxone after confirming no prior history of reaction to this drug.
She is admitted to the intensive care unit for further monitoring.
